summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — OKTA +12%, GNRC +11%, PANW +9%, AKAM +9%, TJX +9%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (HUM -12%, UNH -11%, CNC -7%, ELV -7%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: HUM (-12.12%) — Managed-care selloff on a proposed CMS Medicare Advantage audit rule (extrapolating overpayment recoveries back to 2018; ~$9B/yr est.). Sources date the drop Nov 18, so the Nov 19 date is unconfirmed. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: HUM is a large-cap managed-care name that no strategy includes. It was also a gap-down regulatory shock with no prior signal, which momentum and mean-reversion filters wouldn't catch, and the bot can't short.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Nov 19 catalyst found. Likely a software/cybersecurity sector rally or continued post-S&P 500 inclusion (Nov 4) momentum; earnings are not due until Dec 1.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: OKTA is a mid/large-cap software name that no strategy's universe covers. With no earnings or news gap, a news-reactive trigger would also have had nothing to fire on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add recent S&P 500 additions such as OKTA (effective Nov 4) to the momentum universe, or add a rule that admits any name with a daily move of at least +8% on volume of at least 2x its 20-day average.
